comparison: Both evaluate the core redox regulation claims (C13-C18, C3-C4, C89) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from multiple experimental systems and dose-response relationships. Peer reviewers provide explicit affirmation, with the editor noting 'convincing evidence' and Reviewer 1 calling it 'a very sound biochemical case.' OpenEval includes C19, C21-C22 (cellular chronic oxidative stress data) which peer reviewers evaluate separately in R2.

Partial overlap on cellular validation claims (C19, C21-C22). OpenEval groups these with broader redox regulation evidence in R1, while peer reviewers evaluate cellular Tau phosphorylation and GSH rescue experiments separately. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED, with reviewers noting the authors are 'very clear with the caveats' about connecting in vitro and cellular data.

Both evaluate intramolecular disulfide bond evidence (C23-C24, C26-C27, C50-C51, C91) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes mass spectrometry evidence and structural localization. Peer reviewers provide explicit endorsement, with the editor stating data provide 'convincing evidence that intramolecular disulfide bonds serve a repressive regulatory role.' High agreement (87.5% claim overlap).

Both evaluate CPE motif evolutionary conservation (C35, C45-C46, C48) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes sequence analysis showing BRSK-specific features and evolutionary conservation. Peer reviewers accept the finding, with Reviewer 1 noting identification of 'highly-conserved, but BRSK-specific, Cys residues.' OpenEval includes C36 and C47 (rarity analysis) not explicitly mentioned in peer R8, which also covers C40.

Perfect agreement on CPE-Cys mutation increasing activity (C5, C58, C65). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED with identical claim sets. OpenEval cites quantitative measurements from in vitro and cellular experiments. Peer reviewers accept the finding, with the editor noting the study shows mutation 'increases catalytic activity in vitro and drives phosphorylation.' Reviewer 2 initially questioned mechanism but confirmed concerns were 'satisfactorily addressed.'

Both address MD simulation mechanistic claims (C7, C70-C76) but differ in evaluation. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, emphasizing clear mechanistic basis for CPE-Cys regulation through salt bridge disruption. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 initially concerned that 'no functional evidence of the impact of the salt-bridge network is provided.' While reviewers noted concerns were 'satisfactorily addressed' after revision, the initial critique suggests mechanistic interpretation from simulations alone was viewed as incomplete.

Perfect agreement on T-loop +2 Cys essentiality (C54-C55, C64). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED with identical claim sets. OpenEval notes evidence from in vitro kinase assays and cellular experiments showing reduced basal activity and loss of redox responsiveness. Peer reviewers accept as part of overall redox regulation mechanism without specific critique.

Perfect agreement on HRD-proximal cysteines (C57, C62, C68-C69). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED with identical claim sets. OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from kinase assays, thermal stability, and cellular expression data. Peer reviewers do not challenge findings, with Reviewer 1 implicitly accepting as part of 'a very sound biochemical case' for multiple Cys residues.

Perfect agreement on LKB1-dependent activation control experiments (C28-C30). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED with identical claim sets. OpenEval notes the data establish experimental foundation for mechanistic studies. Peer reviewers do not question these controls, accepting they demonstrate redox regulation operates on top of canonical phosphorylation-dependent activation.

Perfect agreement on glutathionylation evidence (C52-C53). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED with identical claim sets. OpenEval notes immunoblot data supporting multiple redox-active cysteines. Peer reviewers do not challenge the finding, accepting it as consistent with multilayered redox regulation mechanism.

Perfect agreement on C-lobe Cys negative control (C56, C67). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED with identical claim sets. OpenEval notes consistency with structural location and specificity demonstration. Peer reviewers accept as negative control helping define which Cys residues are functionally important.

Both evaluate evidence for multiple cysteines mediating oxidation (C60, C66) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes that CPE-Cys contributes but other cysteines (likely T-loop +2) also mediate oxidative inhibition. Peer reviewers accept as part of multilayered redox regulation, with Reviewer 2 confirming concerns were 'satisfactorily addressed.' OpenEval also includes C59 not in peer R9.

Both evaluate thermal stability data (C61, C63) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes modest Tm changes suggest cysteine effects primarily affect catalytic activity rather than global stability. Peer reviewers accept findings as supporting interpretation that redox regulation operates through conformational effects on active site. OpenEval includes C62 not in peer R15; peer R15 excludes C62.

Perfect agreement on RMSF simulation data (C77). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED with identical claim sets. OpenEval notes the somewhat surprising result that disulfide formation doesn't cause large conformational changes. Peer reviewers do not challenge the simulation result, though Reviewer 2 initially questioned broader mechanistic interpretation from simulations.

Both evaluate oligomerization evidence (C78-C83) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes that oligomerization occurs but monomers predominate, leading to inference it's not the primary inhibition mechanism. Peer reviewers accept the data without challenge, focusing comments on primary intramolecular disulfide mechanism. OpenEval R16 covers C78-C83; peer R10 covers C78-C88 (includes additional SEC-MALS claims).

Both evaluate dimerization capacity evidence (C84-C88) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes co-IP and SEC-MALS data showing primarily monomeric BRSKs with capacity to form dimers. Peer reviewers accept without challenge. OpenEval R17 focuses on C84-C88; peer R10 groups these with C78-C83 (oligomerization claims) in a single evaluation.

Divergent evaluations of broader implications (C8, C93-C94). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting that while sequence analysis is supported, the functional claim about broader prevalence of disulfide regulation is speculative without experimental validation in other kinases. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting evolutionary analysis and broader implications, with the editor noting findings 'will be of broad interest' and have therapeutic implications. Peer R11 also includes C44, C47, C49 not in OpenEval R20.

Partial overlap on evolutionary/phylogenetic analysis (C40, C45-C46). OpenEval R10 evaluates comprehensive sequence analysis across ARK family (C37-C40, C44-C46) as SUPPORTED. Peer R8 evaluates evolutionary conservation and BRSK-specific features (C35-C36, C40, C45-C46, C48) as SUPPORTED. Both accept the phylogenetic context, though they group different claim combinations.

Partial overlap on evolutionary implications (C40-C43, C49). OpenEval R19 evaluates phylogenetic analysis and correlation between BRSK evolution and Cys accumulation as SUPPORTED, noting functional significance requires experimental validation. Peer R11 evaluates broader evolutionary analysis (C8, C44, C47, C49, C93-C94) as SUPPORTED, accepting therapeutic implications. Limited claim overlap (only C49).

Minimal overlap on protein stability interpretation (C20). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting the decrease in protein levels could reflect multiple mechanisms beyond simple stability loss, requiring additional experiments. Peer R2 evaluates cellular validation broadly (C19-C22) as SUPPORTED, accepting the authors' caveats about connecting in vitro and cellular data. Peer reviewers do not specifically critique the C20 stability interpretation.

OpenEval evaluates basic cellular assay validation (C11-C12) as SUPPORTED, noting western blot data clearly shows BRSK-dependent Tau phosphorylation abolished in kinase-dead mutants. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these foundational assay validation claims.

OpenEval evaluates background citations (C31-C34) as SUPPORTED, noting they accurately cite prior work on T-loop +2 Cys conservation and redox regulation in related kinases. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature context claims.

OpenEval evaluates foundational background knowledge (C1-C2, C9-C10) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations for established understanding of kinase regulation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these general background claims.

OpenEval evaluates ARK family background (C96-C104) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations for established knowledge about ARK family structure, regulation, and biological functions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these extensive background context claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims about multiple reactive cysteines and BRSK-NRF2 connection (C90, C92) as SUPPORTED, citing experimental data and prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluates structural background on conserved salt bridge (C95) as SUPPORTED, noting accurate citation of established structural knowledge providing context for CPE-Cys oxidation effects. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this structural context claim.

Minimal overlap (C47 only). OpenEval R3 evaluates CPE motif sequence analysis and BRSK-specific features (C35-C36, C45-C48) as SUPPORTED. Peer R11 evaluates broader evolutionary analysis and therapeutic implications (C8, C44, C47, C49, C93-C94) as SUPPORTED. Different focus despite single shared claim about Cys rarity at this position.

Minimal overlap (C62 only). OpenEval R14 evaluates thermal stability data (C61-C63) as SUPPORTED. Peer R7 evaluates HRD-proximal cysteines functional importance (C57, C62, C68-C69) as SUPPORTED. C62 appears in both but in different functional contexts (thermal stability vs. HRD mutant effects).
